intro: Lesson 32: Non-fiction and grammar: a shipwreck news report with colons and semi-colons. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Teacher-written practice news report (an invented event)
paras: SAILOR RESCUED AFTER TWO DAYS ADRIFT
A fisherman was rescued off the Cornish coast yesterday after spending 48 hours clinging to an upturned boat. The 52-year-old was spotted by a coastguard helicopter at dawn; he was cold but unhurt.
"I kept talking to myself," he said. "I had one thought: get home."
The boat capsized in a sudden squall on Tuesday evening.

head: Colon (:)
Semi-colon (;)
rows: an explanation: 'I had one thought: get home.'
'he was cold but unhurt' after a semi-colon
a list: 'He had three things: rope, water, hope.'
each side could be a sentence
what comes before must be a full clause

blocks.h: Model: a lead for Alonso's shipwreck

model.title: Write a lead: King Alonso's ship wrecked near an island.

parts.text: Who: King Alonso of Naples and his court
What: shipwrecked in a violent storm
Where and when: near a remote island, yesterday
Add a colon: one surprising detail
Add a semi-colon: link two facts

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: King Alonso of Naples was shipwrecked near a remote island yesterday after a violent storm; his son Ferdinand is missing. Survivors report one strange detail: their clothes are perfectly dry.

keywords.def: the short title of a news story
the first paragraph: who, what, where, when, why
a mark (:) that introduces an explanation or list
a mark (;) that joins two closely linked main clauses

questions.q: Punctuate: 'The rescuers found three things a lifejacket a rope and a flare.'
questions.a: The rescuers found three things: a lifejacket, a rope and a flare.

questions.q: Join with a semi-colon: 'Ferdinand swam ashore. He believed his father had drowned.'
questions.a: Ferdinand swam ashore; he believed his father had drowned.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a headline and a two-paragraph report on Alonso's shipwreck. Use one colon and one semi-colon. Starter: 'King Alonso of Naples...'
questions.a: Headline, a 5W lead, a quotation from a survivor (e.g. Gonzalo), one correct colon and one correct semi-colon.

questions.q: Extend: underline your colon and semi-colon and explain each job.
questions.a: Colon introduces an explanation or list; semi-colon joins two linked clauses.

questions.q: Stretch: how would Prospero's version of the event differ?
questions.a: He would present it as a plan, not a disaster.

options: The storm ended; the island was silent.
questions.a: B) The storm ended; the island was silent.. B joins two main clauses; C splits one clause; A needs a colon for a list.

questions.q: 'I had one thought: get home.' The colon...
Answer the ponder: what can a report do that a play cannot?
questions.a: A report gives facts quickly and neutrally; a play shows feelings and lets us see inside characters.
